A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DBCARE research. Their text, equations, figures, algorithm and Appendices A-E are readable and support comparison, including material relocated between the appendix and main text.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E report original simulations and algorithm evaluations using outcome distributions constructed from published secukinumab trial data.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix E retain these original simulation and drug-discovery evaluation results, with the drug experiment now presented in the main text.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same dynamic budgets, sampling of surviving arms, confidence-based elimination, stopping conditions and recommendation rule. The risk-specific budget and confidence parameters are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate two-arm Gaussian and Bernoulli problems, K-arm Gaussian problems with 1-sparse and linear-decay means, and binary and leveled drug-efficacy outcomes. Moving the drug experiment from Appendix E to Section 4 adds no dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain Sequential Halving and fixed-confidence elimination/racing comparators, with the gap-aware oracle additionally included in the two-arm simulations. Newly cited related methods are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: The reward distributions, gap and cost ranges, arm counts, risk metrics, budget choices, confidence targets and 10/c sampling safeguard are retained. The relocated drug experiment uses the same outcome encoding and population proportions.

E4.justification: The gap, arm-count, reward-structure and sampling-cost sweeps and drug-discovery case study are retained. Removing the enlarged duplicate of the two-arm plots removes no analysis.

E5.justification: Both report 100,000 runs with different random seeds for the two-arm simulations and 10,000 for the K-arm and drug experiments, with uncertainty displayed as empirical averages plus or minus two standard errors. The bands in v2 Figure 2 were already reported in v1 Figure 3.

E6.justification: Matched empirical curves, bars, uncertainty displays and reported findings are unchanged. In particular, v1 Figure 6 becomes v2 Figure 3 with the same drug-experiment results, and Figures 4-5 retain the K-arm results. Plot resizing and the corrected metric label do not establish different outcomes.

T1.justification: The model assumptions, risk definitions, Theorems 1-4, corollaries, oracular propositions and proofs in Appendices A-D are retained. The expanded proof overview in Section 1.2 explains the existing optimization over expected stopping time without changing the derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary and conclusion retain the same risk-based BAI formalism, phase-transition claims, near-optimality guarantees and empirical positioning. Promoting the drug experiment does not expand these claims.

C2.justification: Section 1.3 adds a distinction between exogenous sampling costs and cumulative-regret objectives. The relocated drug discussion omits v1's qualification about conventional designs for late-stage clinical trials and its proposed applicability to early-stage animal testing and high-throughput experiments. The theoretical limitations in the conclusion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both retain the same hardware, approximately 7.5-hour runtime, data-generation details, outcome encoding and hyperparameters. The confidence-bound formula repeated in v2's drug paragraph was already specified for the elimination procedure in v1 Appendix E; it does not introduce a new implementation.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 adds Degenne et al. and Yang et al. on regret-aware BAI, explaining the distinction from exogenous sampling costs, and adds Poiani et al.'s Optimal Multi-Fidelity Best-Arm Identification. This is a limited expansion of positioning; other reference changes largely consolidate duplicate entries or update bibliographic details.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization remain intact. v2 clarifies the lower-bound proof overview, moves and lightly condenses the drug experiment into Section 4, removes the redundant plot-reproduction discussion and adds funding acknowledgments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts NeurIPS styling and resizes and relocates existing figures while retaining their plot types. It incorporates the existing uncertainty bands into Figure 2, removes the enlarged duplicate, moves the drug figure into the main text and places both K-arm figures on one page. The Bernoulli MI axis label is corrected from RSR to RMI.

improvement.justification: The clearer proof overview, more precise comparison with regret-aware BAI and corrected metric label modestly improve explanation and accuracy. Bringing the existing drug experiment into Section 4 makes the empirical support easier to locate. These gains are limited by unchanged scientific evidence, smaller figure displays and the loss of clinical-applicability context.
